What to plant in your state

Quick answer: The rains reach the South first (March to April) and the far North last (June), so the right planting month depends on your state. Pick your state for its own calendar and a live rain check.

North-West

  • Sokotorains June – September
  • Zamfararains June – September
  • Katsinarains June – September
  • Kanorains June – September
  • Jigawarains June – September
  • Kebbirains June – September
  • Kadunarains May – October

North-East

  • Yoberains June – September
  • Bornorains June – September
  • Bauchirains May – October
  • Gomberains May – October
  • Adamawarains May – October
  • Tarabarains April – October

North-Central

  • Nigerrains April – October
  • Kwararains April – October
  • FCTrains April – October
  • Nasarawarains April – October
  • Plateaurains April – October
  • Kogirains April – October
  • Benuerains April – October

South-West

  • Oyorains March – November (two peaks)
  • Osunrains March – November (two peaks)
  • Ekitirains March – November (two peaks)
  • Ogunrains March – November (two peaks)
  • Ondorains March – November (two peaks)
  • Lagosrains March – November (two peaks)

South-East

  • Anambrarains March – November (two peaks)
  • Enugurains March – November (two peaks)
  • Ebonyirains March – November (two peaks)
  • Imorains March – November (two peaks)
  • Abiarains March – November (two peaks)

South-South

  • Edorains March – November (two peaks)
  • Cross Riverrains March – November (two peaks)
  • Deltarains March – November (two peaks)
  • Akwa Ibomrains March – November (two peaks)
  • Bayelsarains February/March – November (very wet)
  • Riversrains February/March – November (very wet)

Written by students of the ByteBusters Coding Club, Yewa College, Ilaro from facts checked against IITA, NAERLS, NRCRI, NIHORT and FAO. Last updated 2026-11-11. A guide, not a promise: always confirm dates with your ADP extension officer.
